page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server powered by a 64-core Ampere Altra processor based on the arm64 architecture. Operating at a dedicated 2.8 GHz clock speed across 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading overhead, the instance is allocated 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps under the KVM hypervisor. It includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent operational volumes.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the strengths and limitations of the high-density Arm core deployment. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core scaling, reaching 114,420.62 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 418.6 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In-memory throughput is notable in cached environments, recording 4,547.79 GB/sec in small-block cached read tests and 84.36 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Single-threaded metrics are more moderate, with stress-ng single-core achieving an average 1,789.29 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling within the bottom tier at 8.38 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency for the ecs.c6r.16xlarge stems from its high physical core density and power-efficient Arm architecture, delivering lower operational overhead per vCPU compared to legacy x86 equivalents. However, workloads requiring specialized x86 vector extensions or high single-thread performance face efficiency compromises. The instance is well matched for highly parallel compute workloads, distributed container clusters, continuous integration builds, in-memory caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture, powered by a 64-vCPU dedicated Ampere Altra processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 128 GB of memory, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes a 16 Gbps baseline network interface, zero bundled local storage, and no hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached disks for persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving 114,420.62 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 418.6 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 84.36 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect moderate execution speeds, with weak single-core bzip3 decompression throughput. Given its architectural profile, ecs.c6r.16xlarge offers resource density and power-efficient parallel compute suited for scale-out container platforms, multi-threaded batch processing, in-memory data caches, and continuous integration pipelines.
